item.title: Māra: You will not escape, You will not escape this world. What use is this practice of seclusion to you? Enjoy sensual pleasures — Do…
item.description:
Māra:

You will not escape,
You will not escape this world.
What use is this practice of seclusion to you?
Enjoy sensual pleasures —
Do not have regrets later.

Elder Nun Selā:

Sensual pleasures are like swords and spears —
They cut the aggregates to pieces.
What you call the pleasure of life —
For me, that sensual pleasure
Is no longer enticing.

Everywhere, delight is destroyed.
The mass of darkness,
The blinding darkness, has been shattered.
Know this, O Evil One —
You are Māra,
You are defeated.

From: Therīgāthā 3.7
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, form is burning; feeling is burning; perception is burning; formations are burning; consciousness is burning. Seeing thus, monks, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted…
item.description:
“Monks, form is burning; feeling is burning; perception is burning; formations are burning; consciousness is burning. Seeing thus, monks, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form … with feeling … with perception … with formations … with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. In liberation, knowledge arises: ‘Liberated.’ He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.61
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Sunakkhatta, suppose there is a bronze cup of drink, beautiful and fragrant, but mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not…
item.description:
“Sunakkhatta, suppose there is a bronze cup of drink, beautiful and fragrant, but mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering. What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Would that man drink from that bronze cup if he knew: ‘If I drink from this, I will meet death or deadly suffering’?”
“No, venerable sir.”
“So too, Sunakkhatta, a monk should surely guard himself in regard to the six sense-bases. Knowing that ‘Attachment is the root of suffering,’ he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment. It does not happen that he would still focus his body on attachment or direct his mind to attachment.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 105 – Sunakkhattasutta

item.title: “Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust…
item.description:
“Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. For direct knowledge of craving, monks, these ten things should be developed.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.237
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “What is the cause, good sirs, what is the condition for the arising of unarisen greed, and for the growth and increase of arisen greed?”…
item.description:
“What is the cause, good sirs, what is the condition for the arising of unarisen greed, and for the growth and increase of arisen greed?” - “The sign of the beautiful.” For one who attends unwisely to the sign of the beautiful, unarisen greed arises and arisen greed increases and grows. This, good sirs, is the cause, this is the condition for the arising of unarisen greed and for the growth and increase of arisen greed.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.68
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, king fights with king, noble warrior…
item.description:
“Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, king fights with king, noble warrior fights with noble warrior, brahmin fights with brahmin, householder fights with householder, mother fights with child, child fights with mother, father fights with child, child fights with father, brother fights with brother, brother fights with sister, sister fights with brother, friend fights with friend. Having engaged in quarrels, disputes, and battles, they attack one another with fists, with stones, with sticks, with swords. There they meet death or deadly suffering. Monks, such is the peril of sensuality, a mass of suffering visible here and now, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis – simply because of sensuality.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 13 – Mahādukkhakkhandhasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, for direct knowledge of greed, six things should be developed. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception…
item.description:
“Monks, for direct knowledge of greed, six things should be developed. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. For direct knowledge of greed, monks, these six things should be developed.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.142

item.title: “What leads the world along? What torments itself? And what is the one thing Upon which everything depends?” “Craving leads the world along, Craving torments…
item.description:
“What leads the world along?
What torments itself?
And what is the one thing
Upon which everything depends?”

“Craving leads the world along,
Craving torments itself,
Craving is the one thing
Upon which everything depends.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.63
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Householder, the form element is the home of consciousness. Consciousness bound by lust for the form element, householder, is called ‘wandering with a home.’ The…
item.description:
“Householder, the form element is the home of consciousness. Consciousness bound by lust for the form element, householder, is called ‘wandering with a home.’ The feeling element is the home of consciousness. Consciousness bound by lust for the feeling element … The perception element … The formation element … The consciousness element is the home of consciousness. Consciousness bound by lust for the consciousness element, householder, is called ‘wandering with a home.’ Thus, householder, is wandering with a home.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.3

item.title: Who has conquered the thorn of sensuality, Insult, injury, bondage, That one stands firm, Like a mountain unshaken — Such a monk, Pleasure and pain…
item.description:
Who has conquered the thorn of sensuality,
Insult, injury, bondage,
That one stands firm,
Like a mountain unshaken —
Such a monk,
Pleasure and pain do not disturb.

From: Udana 3.3
